body:
## Summary

Adds `retrySend?: boolean` to `ClientOptions` (default `false`). When enabled, `send()` (POST) uses the client's existing retries and exponential backoff for 5xx and network/timeout errors. 401, 413, 429 and other 4xx responses still fail immediately.

The default stays non-retrying because pre-1.0 servers may not deduplicate identical messages.

## Tests

- `npm test` — 36 passed, including new cases for 503 retry, timeout retry, no retry on 401/413/429, and default-off behavior
- `npm run lint` — passed
- `npm run build` — passed (ESM, CJS, and declarations)

`npm run format:check` fails on both this branch and current `main` due a pre-existing Prettier config mismatch, and is not part of CI.

Closes #82.

AI assistance was used to implement and verify the change; I reviewed the full diff locally.

No separate issue. This fixes the failed 1.1.0 release: [Version Release run 40285482979](https://github.com/AOSSIE-Org/ThruBox-Client/actions/runs/40285482979/job/121448071795).

###  Screenshots/Recordings:

Simulated locally against the real `v1.1.0` tag:

```
tag VERSION file: [1.1.0]                 -> existing tag is reused
build from v1.1.0: 30 tests pass, DTS build ok
mkdir -p + npm pack -> aossie-org-thrubox-client-1.1.0.tgz

```

###  Additional Notes:

**What failed:** merging #65 tagged `v1.1.0` and published the GitHub release. The `build` job then failed in **Pack package**, because `npm pack --pack-destination /tmp/pack` does not create the directory (`ENOENT`). `publish` was skipped, so **1.1.0 is not on npm**. A plain re-run can't fix this: it uses the same workflow file, and a new run would stop at "Tag v1.1.0 already exists".

**Changes to `version-release.yml`:**
- `mkdir -p /tmp/pack` before `npm pack`.
- **Re-runs can finish an interrupted release:**
  - An existing `vX.Y.Z` tag is reused, but only if its `VERSION` file matches.
  - The GitHub release step is skipped if the release is already published.
  - The package is **built from the tag**, so what reaches npm is exactly the released code.
  - `npm publish` is skipped if that version is already on npm.
- The release job only runs on `main`, including manual runs. CodeRabbit raised this on AOSSIE-Org/ThruBox-Server#67.

**After merging:** run **Actions → Version Release → Run workflow** on `main`. It reuses `v1.1.0`, skips the GitHub release, builds from the tag and publishes `@aossie-org/thrubox-client@1.1.0`.

⚠️ **npm Trusted Publishing must be configured.** Every earlier release run (August) failed at `npm publish` with `E404 Not Found - PUT`, which is how npm reports that the workflow isn't authorised to publish. body:
###  Addressed Issues:
<!-- Link the issue this PR addresses -->
Fixes #64

Companion to AOSSIE-Org/ThruBox-Server#67, which gives every message a per-mailbox `seq` and adds `?after=` / `?limit=` to `GET /api/messages/{address}`.

###  Screenshots/Recordings:

Built SDK (`dist/`) against a ThruBox Server built from #67:

```
PASS  seq assigned per mailbox  (1, 2)
PASS  id is a 64-char hash
PASS  identical resend returns the existing message
PASS  mailbox holds two messages
PASS  receive after=1 returns only the second
PASS  receive limit=1 returns only the first
PASS  seq is not reused after deleting the newest message  (got 3)
PASS  poll with cursor delivers each message once  ([["one","three"],["four"],[]])
```

###  Additional Notes:

**API changes (all additive):**
- `Message.seq?: number`. It's optional because older servers don't send it. The `id` doc no longer promises a UUID, since IDs are now content hashes. Treat them as opaque.
- `receive(address, { after?, limit? })`. A new `ReceiveOptions` type is exported.
- `poll(address, callback, { after })` opts into cursor tracking. Each poll fetches only messages with `seq > cursor`, and **the cursor advances only after the callback returns or its promise resolves**. If the callback throws or rejects, the same messages are delivered again on the next poll, so a failed save is retried rather than silently skipped.

**Behaviour changes in `poll()`, for every caller:**
- The callback is now awaited before the next poll is scheduled, so an async callback can no longer overlap with the next poll.
- A callback that throws is reported to `onError` and polling continues. Previously a synchronous throw rejected the internal loop and stopped polling silently.

**Compatibility:**
- Without `after`, `poll()` passes the whole mailbox every time, exactly as before. Chainvoice (which dedupes by message ID and relies on retrying a message whose handler failed) works unchanged. It can opt in to the cursor later.
- Against an older server, `seq` is undefined, so the cursor never advances and the server ignores `?after`. Every poll returns the full mailbox, same as today.
- No breaking changes. This PR does **not** change the version; the release is cut from #65 (see below).

**Release pipeline (the release itself is cut from #65):**
- **No version change here.** `VERSION`, `package.json` and `package-lock.json` stay at 1.0.2, so merging this PR does not release anything. #65, which is stacked on this PR, bumps to **1.1.0**, so cursors and the removal of `delete()` ship together, and `VERSION` changes on `main` only once.
- **Release notes are a GitHub draft release** ([v1.1.0 draft](https://github.com/AOSSIE-Org/ThruBox-Client/releases), visible to maintainers). It has highlights, a cursor-polling diagram, an example and a compatibility table. I made it by editing Release Drafter's existing `v1.0.3` draft in place; no release or tag was deleted.
- **`version-release.yml`** now publishes the draft named `vX.Y.Z` (or any draft, as a fallback), keeping its notes and appending GitHub's generated "What's Changed" list. Previously, with no draft, the release only said "This release was automatically created…", which is what v1.0.2 shows.
- **Release Drafter now runs manually only.** It rewrote the draft on every push to `main` and would have overwritten the hand-written notes, possibly in the same push that publishes them. The workflow and its config are kept.
- ⚠️ Until this PR merges, the old Release Drafter still runs on every push to `main`. If anything else merges first, it will overwrite the v1.1.0 draft. Merge this PR first, then #65.

**Dependency fix, required for the publish to work:** `npm ci` has been failing on `main`, and `version-release.yml` runs `npm ci` before `npm publish`, so a release would currently fail. Two conflicts caused it:
- `@vitest/coverage-v8` 5.x requires vitest 5, but vitest was still `^3.2`.
- `typescript ^7.0.2` is outside typescript-eslint's peer range (`>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`). TypeScript 6.0 is in range, but tsup's declaration build then fails, because tsup sets `baseUrl` and TypeScript 6 rejects it as deprecated.

Fix: pin `typescript` to `~5.9.3`, the version 1.0.2 was released with, and take the pending Dependabot bumps together so the tree resolves. This supersedes #57, #58, #59, #60 and #61, which Dependabot will close once this is merged:

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| typescript | ^7.0.2 | ~5.9.3 |
| vitest | ^3.2.0 | ^5.0.5 (#60) |
| @vitest/coverage-v8 | ^5.0.0 | ^5.0.5 (#58) |
| eslint | ^10.5.0 | ^10.12.0 (#57) |
| typescript-eslint | ^8.61.1 | ^8.71.2 (#59) |
| prettier | ^3.5.0 | ^3.9.10 (#61) |

With these, a clean `npm ci`, the tests (28/28), `tsc --noEmit` and the tsup build (ESM, CJS and DTS) all pass. Dependabot will offer TypeScript 7 again; leave it unmerged until typescript-eslint supports it.

**Tests:** 10 new tests covering the query string (including `after=0`), the cursor advancing, redelivery after a rejected callback, polling continuing after a synchronous throw or a throwing `onError`, a callback that empties its array, polling waiting for a pending async callback, no cursor when `after` is unset, and validation of invalid `after` values. All 31 tests pass and `tsc --noEmit` is clean. `npm run lint` reports one error, at `src/client.ts:60` (`preserve-caught-error` in the constructor). v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

Release notes

Sourced from actions/github-script's releases.

v9.0.0

New features:

  • getOctokit factory function — Available directly in the script context. Create additional authenticated Octokit clients with different tokens for multi-token workflows, GitHub App tokens, and cross-org access. See Creating additional clients with getOctokit for details and examples.
  • Orchestration ID in user-agent — The ACTIONS_ORCHESTRATION_ID environment variable is automatically appended to the user-agent string for request tracing.

Breaking changes:

  • require('@actions/github') no longer works in scripts. The upgrade to @actions/github v9 (ESM-only) means require('@actions/github') will fail at runtime. If you previously used patterns like const { getOctokit } = require('@actions/github') to create secondary clients, use the new injected getOctokit function instead — it's available directly in the script context with no imports needed.
  • getOctokit is now an injected function parameter. Scripts that declare const getOctokit = ... or let getOctokit = ... will get a SyntaxError because JavaScript does not allow const/let redeclaration of function parameters. Use the injected getOctokit directly, or use var getOctokit = ... if you need to redeclare it.
  • If your script accesses other @actions/github internals beyond the standard github/octokit client, you may need to update those references for v9 compatibility.
